claude.performance_metric: no divestiture; BEA products retained and integrated into Oracle Fusion Middleware (WebLogic made strategic Java app server)
claude.rationale: Deal structure (§2) was a whole-entity, same-industry statutory merger: T4 product (WebLogic/BEA franchise), T5 development/support processes, and T6 workforce all transferred together into Oracle's Fusion Middleware organization, with no documented product-vs-process or process-vs-organization structural mismatch at closing, so gap_45=0 and gap_56=0. On outcome (§3-4), P4 product-process disruption is explicitly "None documented" (Oracle published an orderly product-categorization roadmap rather than abrupt discontinuation), yielding p4_pathway=0; P5 process-organization fracture is marked "None documented"/UNVERIFIED, so under conservative coding p5_pathway=0. T1 and T2 channels were documented as complementary same-industry with no incoherence, both coded 0.

gemini.performance_metric: No divestiture; BEA's products were retained and integrated into Oracle Fusion Middleware
gemini.rationale: The dossier documents that BEA's product franchise transferred (T4) alongside its product-development and support operations (T5), which were integrated into Oracle's Fusion Middleware organization, resulting in no structural gap at closing (gap_45 = 0). BEA's workforce also transferred into Oracle (T6) to support these operations, showing no process-organization mismatch (gap_56 = 0). At the 3-5 year horizon, there is no documented disruption at the product-process interface (p4_pathway = 0), as Oracle successfully executed a product roadmap, nor is there any documented fracture at the process-organization interface (p5_pathway = 0).
